articles.body:

Warburton, 34, who previously played league football for Northampton Town, said he took on the strike when he could not see a pass on, and thought: "Why not?"

articles.title: How to choose the right insoles for your feet, according to podiatrists
articles.summary: Podiatrists give tips on shopping for supportive, comfortable insoles that can help with arch pain, plantar fasciitis and more.
articles.body: If you have a job that requires you to be constantly on your feet, are an avid runner who logs long distances regularly, or are often walking, running or standing, there’s a simple way to make your shoes more comfortable and supportive: add insoles to your running or walking sneakers. Insoles are inserts you can put inside the base of your shoes to increase cushioning, boost arch support and improve fit. But putting the wrong ones in your sneakers can cause discomfort and pain. To help you shop for insoles that work for your feet, I asked podiatrists what to look for and compiled a list of recommendations that align with their guidance The best insoles of 2026 The over-the-counter insoles below were selected with our experts’ criteria in mind. These insoles have a neutral arch (meaning they are medium height), making them suitable for most foot types. They are available in men’s sizes 7-14 and can be trimmed to fit your shoes better. They have gel pads in the heel cup and the forefoot to provide shock absorption and are lightweight, so they won’t add weight to your running sneakers. These insoles have high-density foam in the heel to take some pressure off your arch as you walk. The insoles are available in women’s sizes 6-14.5 and men’s sizes 4-16.5. They are specially made to help those with plantar fasciitis, a common condition that involves inflammation in the tissue that runs down the center of the foot. They have a deep heel cup and a rigid bottom for support. Though these insoles are intended to be used during athletic activities (such as running or at the gym), they can be worn anytime you need extra padding and arch support. They come in men’s sizes 8-14. Rather than trying to get your perfect size, the package comes with a guide that helps you trim them down to the right size for your shoes. The insoles are made with special gel technology that the brand says gently massages your feet as you walk to add comfort. They have a low arch support and a deep heel cup for stability. Dr. Bruce Pinker, a board-certified podiatrist and foot surgeon in New York, says these insoles (also available in men’s sizes) provide a nice amount of cushioning and support for an over-the-counter option. They are also available in women’s sizes 4-13 and are covered in moisture-wicking fibers to keep feet dry. According to the brand, the center of the insole has extra cushioning to absorb shock as you walk, a built-in arch provides support, and the heel cup keeps your foot in place as you walk. Unlike the other insoles on this list, these don’t run the full length of your foot. Instead, they go from the start of your arch to your heel. They are intended for those who struggle with plantar fasciitis; the deep heel cup is cushioned to provide relief from the tightness caused by the foot ailment, and they have a built-in arch for support. These insoles will fit men who wear sizes 8-13. Available in women’s sizes 6.5-12, these insoles have a medium-high arch support and offer moderate cushioning, according to the brand. The sculpted heel cup absorbs impact as you step, and a moisture-wicking top cover prevents odors from sweat. These insoles have rigid bottoms, and are approved by the American Podiatric Medical Association. They’re also available in a version for men. These insoles are intended for those who deal with plantar fasciitis or heel pain. They provide moderate cushioning and have a deep heel cut to support your foot as you step, according to the brand. They are available in different sizes, so you don’t have to trim them like some others on this list. Made specifically for running, these insoles absorb shock, are flexible and come in three different arch support options — low, medium and high. They have a zero heel drop, so they fit inside most running shoes and have a mesh layer for breathability, according to the brand. How I picked the best insoles With so many over-the-counter insoles on the market, knowing what to look for when shopping is helpful. According to the podiatrists we spoke with, these are the key elements you should look for in an insole: Heel cup: Look for a sculpted heel cup, says Pinker. This will ensure your foot is cradled in a supportive way. The heel cup should wrap around the back of your foot without rubbing or irritating it as you walk. Cushioning: One of the biggest benefits of using an insole is that it can provide extra padding to your running or walking sneakers. With this in mind, look for insoles that have adequate cushioning for your needs, says Pinker. The insoles should have a layer of foam or gel for some softness as you step. Rigidity: In addition to cushioning, insoles can provide support. Look for cushioned but semi-rigid insoles — if they are flexible, they won’t have proper support, says Dr. Mohammad Rimawi, a board-certified podiatrist in New York City. If you have flat feet, you can also look for arch support insoles. What are the benefits of insoles? Insoles serve different purposes for different people, “but their main function is the ability to provide the feet with support,” says Rimawi. They can be particularly good for those with flat feet or high arches. “When one suffers from flat feet or too high of an arch, this can distribute weight on the foot in a manner that may leave them more prone to injury and pain,” says Rimawi. “The job of insoles is to provide support and redistribute that weight in a more stable manner.” Even if you don’t have arch issues, insoles can provide more comfort as you walk. “They provide cushioning and support as it offloads pressure points on the foot,” says Pinker. “They can also improve the biomechanics of one’s feet and reduce pain in the feet.” Because of the extra cushioning, they can also be good for those dealing with plantar fasciitis, a condition where your plantar fascia (a thick band of tissue that runs down the length of your foot) gets inflamed. This can happen from working out in shoes with no support, tight calves, carrying excess weight and more. There are many different types of insoles available. They are made from plastic or foam and placed inside your shoes. Over-the-counter insoles provide more generic support and padding. Or, you can have custom insoles made at your podiatrist’s office. “Each person’s foot is unique, and over-the-counter insoles are inherently generic,” says Rimawi. Therefore, you may find that the insoles provide too much support, causing pain, or, inversely, too little support, which doesn’t alleviate symptoms. Custom insoles can help you avoid this.” While custom insoles (also called orthotics) can provide personalized support, over-the-counter insoles can also help. “They can provide cushioning and shock absorption and possibly reduce pain in the heel or arch,” says Pinker. “They aren’t harmful, though they may not be helpful to those with serious foot conditions.” How do you know if you need insoles? “Insoles really do provide support, comfort, shock absorption and protection,” says Rimawi. “Therefore, anyone can benefit from wearing them.” That said, some people benefit from them even more than others. You may benefit from insoles more than most if you have flat feet. “When one has a flat foot, the forces placed on the foot are severely skewed and can lead to pain or injury,” says Rimawi. “Insoles with proper arch support can mitigate this.” “Insoles can also be particularly good for those who deal with pain in the heel or ball of the foot,” says Pinker. This is because insoles can help redistribute your weight so it is not all being placed on whichever area is uncomfortable. Another important thing to know: “Over-the-counter insoles work best in sneakers,” says Rimawi. “Custom insoles, however, can be made to fit in dress shoes, boots and sneakers.” Meet our podiatrists At NBC Selected, we work with experts with specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Mohammad Rimawi is a board-certified podiatrist in New York City.Dr. Bruce Pinker is a board-certified podiatrist and foot surgeon in New York. Why trust NBC Selected? I am a commerce editor at NBC Selected and a journalist who regularly covers health and wellness, among other topics. I have recently written stories on the best snow boots with arch support and the best steel-toe boots. For this story, I spoke with podiatrists about shopping for the best insoles for your feet. articles.title: Na China, membro da delegação de Putin carrega maleta nuclear russa | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente participa de encontro trilateral com os presidentes Donald Trump, dos Estados Unidos, e Xi Jinping, da China, nesta quinta-feira (19).
articles.summary: Presidente participa de encontro trilateral com os presidentes Donald Trump, dos Estados Unidos, e Xi Jinping, da China, nesta quinta-feira (19).
articles.body:
Integrante da delegação russa carrega maleta nuclear de Putin em visita à China — Foto: Reprodução/CBS TV

Um integrante da delegação do presidente Vladimir Putin, da Rússia, foi flagrado carregando a maleta nuclear do país. Na cena, o militar é questionado se a mala carrega, de fato, a tecnologia nuclear russa e responde positivamente. Veja abaixo:

Conhecida como Cheget, a maleta permite que Putin mantenha o comando e controle sobre o arsenal nuclear da Rússia o tempo todo, independentemente de sua localização física.

Putin desembarcou na China na tarde de terça-feira (17), onde vai participar de um encontro trilateral com os presidentes Donald Trump, dos Estados Unidos, e Xi Jinping, da China, nesta quinta-feira (19).

Entre os assuntos em discussão no encontro, que pode impactar o futuro da geopolítica mundial, estão temas delicados, como a proliferação de armas nucleares e guerras.

▶️ Contexto: essa será a primeira vez que os chefes de Estado dos Estados Unidos, da Rússia e da China terão um encontro reservado, cara a cara. A reunião será na cidade chinesa de Shenzhen, durante a cúpula da Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico (Apec).

A Casa Branca afirmou que Trump estará focado em tentar costurar um acordo para reduzir o número de armas nucleares no mundo.

A Rússia afirmou que o encontro será uma demonstração da atual ordem mundial multipolar e destacou que nunca houve uma reunião semelhante.

Já a China disse que o encontro terá um "significado histórico" e contribuirá para a paz e a estabilidade no mundo.

Até agora, o controle de armas nucleares é o único tema confirmado na agenda. Trump também pretende discutir a guerra no Irã.

Já sobre a Ucrânia, houve versões diferentes: inicialmente, o governo americano disse que o assunto ficaria de fora, mas Trump afirmou depois que pretende levá-lo à mesa.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, cumprimenta o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, enquanto o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, está ao lado — Foto: Iori Sagisawa/Pool via REUTERS

articles.title: MPT pede R$ 100 milhões à 99 por cobrança antecipada de motoristas | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministério Público questiona modelo em que trabalhadores pagam para usar a plataforma sem garantia de conseguir corridas suficientes para recuperar o investimento.
articles.summary: Ministério Público questiona modelo em que trabalhadores pagam para usar a plataforma sem garantia de conseguir corridas suficientes para recuperar o investimento.
articles.body:
Motorista de aplicativo — Foto: Maksim Goncharenok/Pexels

O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) entrou na Justiça contra a 99 Tecnologia para pedir a suspensão imediata do programa Taxa Zero , a devolução dos valores pagos por motoristas e o pagamento de uma indenização por danos morais coletivos de R$ 100 milhões.

A ação civil pública foi ajuizada após o lançamento da modalidade, em 9 de junho deste ano, em 25 cidades brasileiras. Conforme a empresa informou ao lançar o programa, ele pode ser ampliado para outras regiões do país.

O Taxa Zero funciona como uma espécie de assinatura. Em vez de ter uma porcentagem descontada de cada corrida, o motorista paga antecipadamente para trabalhar sem a taxa de serviço da plataforma.

Há duas modalidades: uma por período determinado, com validade de 24 ou 72 horas, e outra por ganhos, em que o trabalhador paga um valor para rodar sem cobrança até atingir um limite de faturamento estabelecido pela empresa.

Para o MPT, o modelo transfere aos motoristas um risco que deveria ser assumido pela plataforma . Isso porque a adesão ao programa não garante uma quantidade mínima de corridas nem a recuperação do valor investido.

Pelos próprios termos da 99, a distribuição das viagens continua sendo feita pelo algoritmo do aplicativo e pode contemplar também motoristas que não aderiram ao Taxa Zero.

Diante disso, o órgão sustenta que o trabalhador pode pagar para acessar o sistema sem ter certeza de que conseguirá obter receita suficiente para compensar o gasto.

A ação também questiona o mecanismo de cobrança adotado pela empresa. Segundo o MPT, quando o motorista não possui saldo para quitar o valor devido, a plataforma pode reter automaticamente remunerações futuras .

Para os procuradores responsáveis pelo caso, essa dinâmica cria uma situação de dependência econômica entre trabalhador e empresa e pode configurar o que a legislação classifica como servidão por dívida, quando uma pessoa permanece trabalhando para quitar débitos acumulados.

"O mecanismo de cobrança do Taxa Zero cria uma estrutura objetiva de endividamento permanente: o motorista que não possui saldo suficiente tem suas futuras remunerações retidas automática e integralmente pela ré. Esse mecanismo perpetua a dependência econômica do trabalhador em relação à plataforma e replica, no ambiente digital, a estrutura de servidão por dívida", afirmam os procuradores na ação.

Com base nesse entendimento, o procurador Marcello Ribeiro Silva, que assina a ação, sustenta que a prática pode caracterizar trabalho em condição análoga à escravidão.

O coordenador nacional de combate às fraudes trabalhistas do MPT, Rodrigo Castilho, também criticou o programa.

"Trata-se de uma cobrança abusiva de valores pela 99 em face dos seus motoristas. Essa dinâmica de cobrança gera endividamento ao motorista de app que já começa sua jornada devendo à plataforma e tal condição pode caracterizar o crime de condição análoga à escravidão pela nossa legislação. Por tais motivos, o MPT ingressou com essa medida e estamos confiantes na Justiça para barrar essa funcionalidade ilegal."

Outro ponto levantado pelo Ministério Público envolve as regras de adesão ao programa.

De acordo com a ação, o contrato foi elaborado unilateralmente pela empresa, sem possibilidade de negociação pelos motoristas. O documento também prevê que a 99 pode alterar as regras do Taxa Zero a qualquer momento e desativar o passe adquirido sem devolver os valores pagos.

Além das questões trabalhistas, o MPT argumenta que o modelo pode afetar a concorrência entre aplicativos de transporte. Isso porque o motorista que desembolsa um valor para aderir ao programa tende a concentrar sua atividade na própria 99 para tentar recuperar o investimento feito.

Na visão do órgão, o mecanismo funciona como uma forma indireta de fidelização, reduzindo a liberdade do trabalhador para alternar entre plataformas em busca de melhores condições de trabalho e remuneração.

Além da suspensão do Taxa Zero e da devolução dos valores pagos pelos motoristas, o MPT pediu à Justiça acesso ao código-fonte do algoritmo da empresa . O objetivo é obter informações sobre os critérios usados para distribuir corridas, definir preços e calcular os valores repassados aos trabalhadores.

O processo será analisado pela 1ª Vara do Trabalho de Goiânia.

Procurada, a 99 não havia se manifestado até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Juíza prorroga bloqueio à construção de Arco do Triunfo de Trump | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão impede por mais duas semanas a construção do monumento, que deve ter aproximadamente 76 metros, e ficar localizado nas proximidades do Cemitério Nacional de Arlington.
articles.summary: Decisão impede por mais duas semanas a construção do monumento, que deve ter aproximadamente 76 metros, e ficar localizado nas proximidades do Cemitério Nacional de Arlington.
articles.body:
Uma maquete do arco do triunfo proposto pelo presidente Donald Trump é exibida na Great American State Fair, no National Mall, em Washington. — Foto: Jen Golbeck/AP

A Justiça Federal dos Estados Unidos prorrogou a decisão de impedir que o governo do presidente Donald Trump construa um Arco do Triunfo em Washignton, capital do país.

A decisão, de uma juíza federal, impede por mais duas semanas a construção do monumento, que deve ter aproximadamente 76 metros, e ficar localizado nas proximidades do Cemitério Nacional de Arlington.

Esta é a segunda decisão que barra a promessa de Trump. No dia 6 de novembro, uma juíza federal bloqueou o projeto horas depois de uma comissão pública aprovar a sua construção .

A juíza federal distrital Tanya Chutkan, que supervisiona o caso, determinou que o governo Trump não pode iniciar a construção do monumento por duas semanas, enquanto o tribunal avalia as contestações sobre sua legalidade.

A decisão anterior terminava nesta quinta-feira (19) e foi ampliada pela própria juíza Tanya Chutkan.

O bloqueio ocorreu após a Comissão Nacional de Planejamento da Capital (NCPC) ter aprovado, também na quinta-feira, por 8 votos a 4, o projeto do Arco do Triunfo de Trump, apesar de ter ouvido durante horas os depoimentos de dezenas de opositores que questionavam sua validade e finalidade.

Na oportunidade, a Casa Branca criticou a juíza Chutkan, a quem chamou de "ativista", porém minimizou a suspensão das obras.

"Estamos confiantes de que teremos plena razão ao longo do processo judicial e esperamos ver a conclusão deste magnífico Arco — uma homenagem aos 250 anos de grandeza americana", afirmou em comunicado.

O principal argumento é a localização da estrutura de 76 metros de altura: ao lado do venerado Cemitério Nacional de Arlington, local onde foram enterrados centenas de milhares de militares americanos.

O gigantesco monumento seria significativamente maior que o Arco do Triunfo de Paris, no qual é inspirado. Também seria maior que o Memorial Lincoln, do outro lado do rio Potomac.

A administração Trump sustenta que o Congresso aprovou o arco há mais de 100 anos, quando também autorizou a construção de uma ponte sobre o rio Potomac. O governo argumenta que o arco serviria para homenagear os veteranos.

Os quatro comissários que votaram contra o projeto solicitaram o adiamento da decisão, apontando preocupações jurídicas, a falta de uma verba aprovada pelo Congresso para financiar o projeto e dúvidas sobre as afirmações do secretário de Defesa, Pete Hegseth, sobre o uso militar do arco.

Grupos de preservação histórica e outros autores de ações judiciais estão contestando ativamente vários dos projetos de Trump, alegando que eles contornaram as análises federais, carecem de autorização do Congresso e causam danos a espaços públicos.

A decisão de Chutkan está de acordo com a opinião de veteranos militares e dos procuradores-gerais de Washington e da Virgínia, que haviam apresentado uma ação para impedir a construção do arco.

Desde seu retorno à Casa Branca em janeiro de 2025, Trump estimula projetos de construção e reformas para impor sua marca em Washington.

Entre as obras mais famosas está um salão de baile na Casa Branca, para o qual o magnata republicano mandou demolir uma ala inteira da mansão presidencial.

A Suprema Corte decidiu, por fim, que o autor da ação apresentada para interromper o projeto não tinha legitimidade.

articles.summary: Prefeitura estendeu número de inscrições para que interessados possam concorrer à homologação. Número total de vagas é de 600.
articles.body:
Credenciamento para novos taxistas em Salvador acaba em dezembro — Foto: Bruno Concha/Secom PMS

O credenciamento para novos taxistas em Salvador permanecerá aberto até 17 de dezembro, conforme informado pela Secretaria Municipal de Mobilidade (Semob).

Embora o número de inscritos habilitados já tenha alcançado a quantidade prevista para o processo, novas candidaturas ainda serão aceitas até o encerramento do prazo.

Segundo a Semob, o quantitativo atingido ainda não foi homologado oficialmente. Por isso, pessoas interessadas em ingressar no serviço de táxi na capital baiana continuam podendo participar do credenciamento.

A medida garante que outros candidatos tenham a oportunidade de se inscrever dentro do período estabelecido pelo processo seletivo.

De acordo com o secretário de Mobilidade, Pablo Souza, a expectativa é ampliar a oferta do serviço com a entrada de até 600 novos profissionais.

“Estamos alcançando a meta de 600 novos taxistas, que representam um fortalecimento e recomposição do serviço, que é de fundamental importância para nossa cidade. São famílias que ganham essa oportunidade e a mobilidade gerando inclusão social, emprego e renda”, afirmou.

As regras do credenciamento, a lista de documentos exigidos e as orientações para participação estão disponíveis no site da Semob .

articles.title: GPACI realiza 18ª edição do Natal em Cores em Sorocaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento beneficente ocorreu no Ipanema Clube, e reuniu participantes em prol do atendimento a crianças e adolescentes com câncer.
articles.summary: O espírito natalino e a solidariedade se encontram nesta quarta-feira (18) em Sorocaba (SP), durante a 18ª edição do Natal em Cores.
articles.body:
Hospital Gpaci, em Sorocaba (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

O espírito natalino e a solidariedade se encontram nesta quarta-feira (18), em Sorocaba (SP), durante a 18ª edição do Natal em Cores, tradicional evento beneficente promovido pelo Grupo de Pesquisa e Assistência ao Câncer Infantil (Gpaci). A programação começou às 16h, no Ipanema Clube, e reuniu quase 800 pessoas.

O encontro reúne apoiadores, voluntários, parceiros e integrantes da comunidade em uma tarde de confraternização com um propósito: contribuir com o trabalho desenvolvido pelo hospital no atendimento a crianças e adolescentes com câncer.

A renda arrecadada durante o evento será destinada integralmente ao Hospital Gpaci, ajudando na manutenção das atividades e na continuidade da assistência prestada aos pacientes.

O Natal em Cores é organizado com o envolvimento da diretoria da instituição, voluntários, patronesses e parceiros, que colaboram para a realização de mais uma edição da iniciativa.

O Gpaci é referência regional no atendimento especializado em oncologia pediátrica. A unidade atende crianças e adolescentes de zero a 18 anos, de Sorocaba e outros 47 municípios.

Com apoio de empresas, voluntários e da comunidade, o hospital oferece assistência especializada e humanizada a pacientes e familiares. Eventos beneficentes como o Natal em Cores ajudam a manter a estrutura e os serviços oferecidos pela instituição.

A 18ª edição reforça a mobilização de pessoas em torno da causa, transformando uma celebração de fim de ano em uma iniciativa de apoio ao tratamento e à qualidade de vida de crianças e adolescentes atendidos pelo Gpaci.

articles.title: Policiais da França protestam por aumento e falam em desgaste pós atos | G1
articles.standfirst: Mobilização ocorre após semanas de manifestações sociais e estudantis. Governo promete elevar o benefício gradualmente até 2029, já sindicatos consideram a proposta insuficiente.
articles.summary: A Polícia da França exige reajuste de 35% no adicional de risco e mais efetivo para conter o desgaste físico e mental agravado pela recente onda de manifestações no país.
articles.body:
Policiais entram em confronto com manifestantes no quinto sábado de protestos na França contra o alto custo de vida, em foto de 14 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: Reuters/Benoit Tessier

Dezenas de policiais protestaram nesta quarta-feira (18) em frente ao Ministério do Interior da França para exigir aumento do adicional de risco e mais efetivo nas corporações. A mobilização, convocada pelo sindicato Alliance, ocorre após semanas de manifestações sociais e estudantis que intensificaram a atuação das forças de segurança.

O governo promete elevar o benefício gradualmente até 2029, mas os sindicatos consideram a proposta insuficiente.

A mobilização social e estudantil das últimas semanas colocou a polícia na linha de frente da contenção de manifestações e reacendeu a discussão sobre condições de trabalho, efetivo e remuneração dos agentes.

A insatisfação crescente dentro das forças de segurança francesas levou dezenas de policiais a se concentrarem diante do Ministério do Interior, em Paris, para pressionar o governo por um aumento imediato do adicional de risco pago à categoria.

A mobilização desta quarta-feira é resultado de uma disputa que se arrasta há meses. As organizações sindicais argumentam que o aumento da carga de trabalho, a repetição de confrontos em manifestações e a falta de reposição de efetivo agravaram um quadro de desgaste já existente dentro da Polícia Nacional.

A manifestação dos policiais aconteceu poucas horas antes de uma reunião entre representantes sindicais e o ministro do Interior, Laurent Nuñez. Ao término do encontro, o governo informou que continua trabalhando sobre as propostas apresentadas na semana passada para revalorizar a chamada Indenização Especial de Sujeição da Polícia, um complemento salarial destinado a compensar os riscos associados à profissão.

Segundo o ministério, Nuñez reafirmou o compromisso de formalizar por escrito a intenção do governo de negociar um novo protocolo com as entidades representativas da categoria. A sinalização, porém, não encerrou a crise nem dissipou o descontentamento dos sindicatos.

Na avaliação dos representantes da categoria, a polícia francesa enfrenta simultaneamente déficit de pessoal, exaustão profissional e uma percepção crescente de que o trabalho realizado pelos agentes não recebe o reconhecimento adequado do poder público.

Esse sentimento ficou evidente nos discursos dos participantes do ato, que associaram a reivindicação salarial a um problema mais amplo de condições de trabalho.

Policiais são hostilizados pela população durante protestos A hostilidade enfrentada pela polícia francesa durante manifestações tem raízes tanto políticas quanto históricas. A relação se deteriorou especialmente a partir do movimento dos "coletes amarelos", entre 2018 e 2019, quando organizações de direitos humanos, observadores independentes e meios de comunicação documentaram centenas de feridos em operações de dispersão de protestos.

A França é frequentemente apontada por entidades internacionais como um dos países europeus que mais recorreram ao uso de gás lacrimogêneo, granadas de dispersão e lançadores conhecidos pela sigla LBD, uma arma que dispara balas de borracha de alta velocidade e cujo emprego provocou lesões graves, incluindo mutilações e perda de visão em alguns manifestantes.

A imagem das forças de segurança também foi afetada por episódios que tiveram ampla repercussão nacional, como a morte do adolescente Nahel Merzouk durante uma abordagem policial em 2023 e sucessivas denúncias de controles de identidade considerados discriminatórios por associações antirracistas.

Nas manifestações francesas, também são frequentes cantos de "ACAB", sigla em inglês para "All Cops Are Bastards" ("Todos os policiais são canalhas"), slogan surgido em movimentos contestatórios britânicos e adotado por grupos de esquerda, anarquistas e coletivos antirracistas em diversos países. A expressão aparece regularmente em cartazes, pichações e palavras de ordem durante protestos contra reformas do governo, violência policial e discriminação racial na França.

Sindicatos falam em desgaste e falta de efetivo Sylvia Vaudou, dirigente do sindicato Alliance no departamento do Loire, afirmou que os problemas enfrentados pela corporação se acumulam há anos e se tornaram mais visíveis após os recentes movimentos de protesto.

Segundo ela, a manifestação de 17 de outubro teria deixado um número elevado de policiais feridos, reforçando a percepção de que os agentes são cada vez mais demandados sem que haja reforço proporcional dos quadros da segurança pública.

"Nós estamos desgastados, cansados, e hoje é preciso que o governo nos ouça", afirmou. A dirigente acrescentou que a categoria cobra "muito mais efetivo" e uma valorização do adicional de risco.

A reivindicação pelo aumento do benefício tornou-se o principal ponto de união entre os diferentes sindicatos policiais. Alliance, Un1té e Unsa já haviam se reunido com Laurent Nuñez na sexta-feira passada para apresentar formalmente a demanda, mas deixaram a reunião insatisfeitos com a proposta apresentada pelo governo.

Manifestante carrega cartaz com a frase "Entreguem dinheiro, não policiais" no quinto sábado de protestos na França contra o alto custo de vida, em foto de 14 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: Reuters/Benoit Tessier

Os sindicatos defendem uma valorização de 35% do adicional. Já o Ministério do Interior propôs elevar o índice do benefício para 33,5%, mas de forma escalonada ao longo de três anos, com a primeira etapa prevista para abril de 2027. A proposta foi considerada insuficiente pelas entidades e a divergência transformou a negociação salarial no principal foco de tensão entre a categoria e o governo nas últimas semanas.

Pressão cresce após movimento dos agentes da tropa de choque A mobilização desta quarta-feira ocorreu um dia depois de uma ação coordenada de integrantes das Companhias Republicanas de Segurança, a força de choque da polícia francesa conhecida pela sigla CRS.

Impedidos legalmente de fazer greve, diversos integrantes da corporação recorreram a licenças médicas simultâneas, numa estratégia interpretada pelos sindicatos como forma de expressar o descontentamento sem violar as restrições impostas à categoria.

O episódio foi visto como mais um sinal da deterioração do clima interno nas forças de segurança.

Fabien Bogais, dirigente do Alliance em Paris, afirmou que parte do mal-estar decorre da sensação de que os policiais não recebem apoio suficiente diante da pressão enfrentada nas ruas. "Não se pode dizer que, com tudo o que está acontecendo hoje nas ruas, manifestações e movimentos sociais, a polícia esteja realmente sendo apoiada e reconhecida", afirmou.

Segundo ele, representantes sindicais de diferentes regiões do país viajaram a Paris para demonstrar ao governo a profundidade da insatisfação existente dentro da corporação.

"Estamos aqui hoje para mostrar ao governo, e a quem quiser ouvir, que a polícia está farta", declarou.

Governo tenta negociar em meio a restrições orçamentárias A atual rodada de negociações teve início em 13 de novembro, quando Laurent Nuñez prometeu rever progressivamente o valor do adicional de risco pago aos policiais. O Ministério do Interior argumenta que a implementação gradual é necessária devido às limitações orçamentárias enfrentadas pelo Estado francês. Segundo o governo, a medida poderia ser concluída até 2029, mantendo abertas as negociações sobre os detalhes de sua aplicação.

Os sindicatos, contudo, consideram o cronograma excessivamente longo diante das demandas imediatas da categoria. Para as organizações representativas, a pressão exercida sobre os agentes durante os sucessivos ciclos de protestos sociais exige uma resposta mais rápida do Executivo.

A diferença entre os 35% reivindicados pelos sindicatos e os 33,5% oferecidos pelo governo pode parecer pequena à primeira vista. No entanto, tornou-se símbolo de um conflito mais amplo sobre salários, efetivos e reconhecimento profissional dentro das forças de segurança francesas, um tema que deve continuar mobilizando a categoria nas próximas semanas.

articles.title: Encontro Trump, Putin e Xi: o risco de uma nova divisão do mundo | G1
articles.standfirst: Existe a preocupação de que, mais uma vez, 3 homens, 3 líderes, 3 países - Estados Unidos, China e Rússia - decidam o futuro do mundo.
articles.summary: O encontro entre Trump, Putin e Xi Jinping em Shenzhen levanta temores sobre uma nova divisão de esferas de influência global, deixando a Europa e a Ucrânia em alerta.
articles.body:
O encontro em Shenzhen acendeu uma preocupação sobre o risco do retorno de uma divisão do mundo em esferas de influência e lembra outro momento histórico em que grandes potências tomaram decisões sobre o futuro de outros países.

Winston Churchill - e seu nono ou décimo charuto do dia. Franklin Roosevelt. Josef Stalin. Foi um acontecimento. “O encontro das três potências”. Era fevereiro de 1945. A derrota da Alemanha nazista, praticamente certa. Com a Segunda Guerra perto do fim, Reino Unido , Estados Unidos e União Soviética se reuniram para negociar não só o futuro da Europa, mas as bases da nova ordem mundial. Foi a Conferência de Yalta.

Pois olha a ironia. Yalta é uma cidade na península da Crimeia. Na época, parte da União Soviética. Hoje, território da Ucrânia ocupado pela Rússia . Depois daquele encontro, o mundo foi se dividindo em dois grandes blocos: um liderado pelos americanos, outro pelos soviéticos.

Oitenta e um anos depois, não existe mais União Soviética. A Rússia herdou parte desse poder. A China virou potência global. Está tudo bem diferente. Os Estados Unidos de Roosevelt continuam na mesa de negociação. Mas o Reino Unido de Churchill perdeu muita força. Está fora das conversas assim como a Europa inteira. Novos tempos.

“ É a Europa em declínio ”, disse ao Jornal Nacional o professor de Política Externa Vuk Vuksanović, do King's College, de Londres. Ele disse que os europeus estão cada vez mais vulneráveis às próprias disfunções internas. E, assim, a Europa vai ficar fora da foto.

Encontro em Shenzhen acende preocupação sobre risco do retorno de divisão do mundo em esferas de influência — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Uma artista na Rússia já imaginou a nova imagem histórica. No lugar de Roosevelt, Churchill e Stalin: Trump, Xi Jinping e Putin. Mas há diferenças fundamentais. Nos anos 1940, eram aliados contra um inimigo em comum: a Alemanha nazista. Hoje, Estados Unidos, China e Rússia têm interesses muitas vezes conflitantes. O jogo é outro, mas a preocupação é a mesma: de que, mais uma vez, três homens, três líderes, três países decidam o futuro do mundo.

Existe uma máxima na diplomacia que diz que, se você não está na mesa de negociação, cuidado: você pode aparecer no cardápio. O medo da Ucrânia é que o mapa do país esteja no menu do encontro, a divisão territorial quando a guerra acabar. Taiwan também está preocupada. Nesse caso, o prato seria servido à China. E não faz muito tempo que Trump jantou a Venezuela. Por isso, a comparação com a Conferência de Yalta voltou a perturbar a diplomacia mundial. Mas será que o encontro de quinta-feira (19) tem mesmo potencial para redefinir o mapa do mundo?

“Embora o simbolismo seja poderoso, eu não espero ver a resolução de grandes conflitos, como o da Ucrânia. Nem um grande acordo sobre a divisão das esferas de influência”, diz Vuk Vuksanović.

Mas o professor sabe que o medo de que isso aconteça é real:

“A comparação com Yalta foi despertada, em grande medida, pelo pânico que existe na Ucrânia de que o encontro possa resultar em um acordo que enfraqueça a posição deles. E também pelo medo na Europa, que vem sendo ignorada por Washington, Pequim e Moscou”.

articles.title: Solidez Engenharia apresenta projeto que integra moradia e lazer em Maceió | G1
articles.standfirst: Park Plaza Murilópolis reúne estrutura de lazer, áreas verdes e localização estratégica na Serraria, com facilidades para a rotina dentro e fora de casa.
articles.summary: Park Plaza Murilópolis reúne estrutura de lazer, áreas verdes e localização estratégica na Serraria, com facilidades para a rotina dentro e fora de casa.
articles.body:
A casa é o ponto de partida de muitas experiências: momentos em família, descanso, convivência e a construção de novas histórias. Pensando nessa relação entre moradia e qualidade de vida, a Solidez Engenharia apresenta o Park Plaza Murilópolis, novo empreendimento residencial localizado no Conjunto Murilópolis, no bairro da Serraria, parte alta de Maceió.

Com 408 apartamentos distribuídos em duas torres, o projeto oferece opções de plantas com dois e três quartos e uma estrutura de lazer e convivência que contempla diferentes perfis de moradores. Piscinas, academia, salão de festas, playground, churrasqueira, quadra esportiva, coworking, espaço de estudos, lavanderia, brinquedoteca e ambientes pet estão entre os espaços planejados para integrar a rotina dos futuros moradores.

Park Plaza Murilópolis – Piscina. — Foto: Solidez Engenharia

O contato com o verde também faz parte da proposta do empreendimento. O projeto contempla pocket parks e paisagismo assinado por Bia Abreu, incorporando áreas verdes aos espaços de convivência e criando ambientes que valorizam o bem-estar, o contato com a natureza e os momentos ao ar livre. A proposta paisagística contribui para uma experiência de moradia que vai além dos espaços internos dos apartamentos.

Park Plaza Murilópolis - Pocket Park — Foto: Solidez Engenharia

A ideia é reunir, em um mesmo endereço, diferentes possibilidades para o dia a dia. Da porta para dentro, os moradores encontram ambientes pensados para o lazer, o descanso, o trabalho e a convivência. Da porta para fora, a localização oferece acesso facilitado a serviços, comércio e conveniências que tornam a rotina mais prática.

Situado atrás do Assaí Atacadista, o empreendimento está próximo a supermercados, escolas, estabelecimentos comerciais e outros serviços essenciais. Ao mesmo tempo, está inserido em uma região residencial, que proporciona um contexto mais tranquilo para quem busca conciliar a praticidade de estar perto de tudo com o conforto de chegar em casa e desacelerar.

Com 22 anos de atuação, a Solidez Engenharia segue desenvolvendo projetos residenciais em Alagoas, buscando aliar estrutura, funcionalidade e localização às necessidades de quem procura um novo lugar para morar.

O Park Plaza Murilópolis está disponível para visitação e apresentação das opções de unidades e condições comerciais.

articles.title: What has happened to the $18bn pledged to Trump’s Board of Peace for Gaza?
articles.summary: Billions have been pledged for Gaza since a 2025 ‘ceasefire’, but rebuilding hasn’t begun and Israeli attacks continue.
articles.body:
Donors have pledged about $18bn for Gaza through US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace. But more than a year after the October 2025 ceasefire, reconstruction has yet to begin, and nearly 1.4 million Palestinians are still living in makeshift shelters.

Even preliminary reconstruction efforts have stalled. The board had asked for $280m to fund the initial building phase, but in September it said most of that money remained unspent.

In its latest report, submitted on Tuesday, the board warned that the truce between Israel and Hamas could collapse unless immediate steps are taken to carry out the ceasefire deal, according to The Associated Press.

The next day, on Wednesday, Israel began its first major military ground operation in the Gaza Strip since the ceasefire began, attacking refugee camps in the central part of the enclave.

Since the ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025, Israel has killed at least 1,658 Palestinians and injured 6,000, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

Israel continues to block the entry of 60,000 mobile homes promised under the ceasefire deal and to severely restrict food and medical aid into the besieged enclave. It has also yet to allow the Palestinian committee set up to administer Gaza to enter the Strip.

United States President Trump proposed the board in September 2025 as part of his 20-point plan for Gaza.

On November 17, 2025, the United Nations Security Council adopted Resolution 2803, which recognised the board as a transitional administration responsible for setting the framework and coordinating funding for Gaza’s redevelopment.

The resolution authorises its role in Gaza until December 31, 2027, unless the UN Security Council decides otherwise. The board’s charter also allows it to work in other areas affected by conflict.

Trump chairs the board and can only be replaced if he resigns or is unable to serve. He also represents the US.

He appoints its executive board, whose members are Ajay Banga, Tony Blair, Martin Edelman, Robert Gabriel Jr, Jared Kushner, Marc Rowan, Marco Rubio, Steve Witkoff, and Susie Wiles.

Each member state has one vote. Decisions need a majority of those present and voting, and Trump’s approval. He can also veto executive board decisions.

Under the plan, Palestinian technocrats would run Gaza’s day-to-day affairs through the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, led by Ali Shaath. The committee reports to the board, but Israel has not allowed it to enter Gaza, and it operates from Cairo.

The board has 28 members: Albania, Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cambodia, Egypt, El Salvador, Hungary, Indonesia, Israel, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kuwait, Mongolia, Morocco, Pakistan, Paraguay, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, the United Arab Emirates, the United States, Uzbekistan, and Vietnam.

Germany, India, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the European Union also attended the inaugural meeting as observers.

Countries join by invitation from Trump and normally serve up to three years. Countries that pay more than $1bn in cash in the charter’s first year are exempt from that limit.

At the board’s first meeting in Washington, DC, on February 19, Trump announced about $7bn in pledges from nine countries, plus a $10bn US pledge. He did not say what the US money would be used for.

The UAE pledged $1.2bn. Kuwait, Qatar and Saudi Arabia pledged $1bn each, with Saudi Arabia saying it would pay over several years. Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Kazakhstan, Morocco, and Uzbekistan also pledged.

What happened to the funding earmarked for Gaza?

At a briefing in New York on September 23, the board said donors had made about $18bn [ pdf ] in early funding commitments. It said it had called in $280m from donors for the building phase so far, and that most of it remained unspent.

Board of Peace officials previously told the Washington Post that the money couldn’t be spent on projects until Israel allowed international troops or newly-trained Palestinian police to enter Gaza and begin the process of disarming Hamas.

The board puts the cost of rebuilding Gaza at about $71bn, close to the UN ’s estimate of $71.5bn, a figure that could rise as more damage is recorded. The board has identified $6bn in projects. It says its six-month recovery plan needs $2.45bn for 66 programmes, plus about $200m in in-kind support.

What does the six-month recovery programme cover?

The 66 programmes are divided across six areas:

Infrastructure development: 24 programmes

The Board of Peace highlights five countries helping Gaza’s recovery on the ground. Others have pledged money, but the board has not said how much each has pledged.

Morocco: Disarming fighters and helping them return to civilian life

United Arab Emirates: Resources, support and its own programmes

articles.title: A Pennsylvania landowner's 4,540-acre forest is protected from subdivision, preserving buffers along three wild-trout streams and public recreation access as a 94-year-old land trust passes 300,000 acres
articles.summary: A forest is rather good at minding its own business.
articles.body: A forest is rather good at minding its own business. Trees grow, streams wind through the undergrowth, wildlife goes about its day and visitors find a little room to breathe. But keeping it that way requires considerably more effort than simply leaving nature alone. One Pennsylvania landowner has taken a significant step towards ensuring that a vast stretch of woodland stays just as it is, protecting thousands of acres from future development.The Western Pennsylvania Conservancy (WPC), a 94-year-old nonprofit conservation organisation, has acquired a conservation easement over a 4,540-acre forest in Sergeant Township, McKean County, Pennsylvania. The agreement prevents the property from being subdivided or developed, safeguarding its forests, waterways and wildlife habitats for generations to come.The announcement, made on November 13, also marks a major milestone for the organisation. With this latest agreement, WPC has permanently protected more than 300,000 acres of land across Western Pennsylvania since its founding in 1932.A forest that will remain a forestThe newly protected property is no ordinary patch of woodland. Spanning 4,540 acres, it is a hilly, heavily forested landscape characterised by deep ravines and a network of waterways. Located within the Clarion River watershed, the property forms part of an extensive natural landscape that supports a variety of wildlife and aquatic habitats.An important feature of the land is its proximity to three streams: Fivemile Run, Sevenmile Run and Rocky Run. The first two flow into the East Branch Clarion River, while Rocky Run feeds into the West Branch Clarion River.All three waterways support naturally reproducing wild trout populations and are recognised as Pennsylvania Wild Trout Waters by the state's Fish and Boat Commission. Fivemile Run and Sevenmile Run also carry the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection's High Quality-Cold Water Fisheries designation.The forest provides important wooded buffers along these streams. These stretches of vegetation are more than just pretty scenery. Trees and other plants along riverbanks help stabilise soil, limit erosion and prevent excess sediment and pollutants from washing into the water. They also provide shade, helping maintain the cooler temperatures that trout need to survive.Protecting the surrounding forest therefore means protecting the conditions that allow these fish populations to thrive.Keeping development at bay without shutting down the forest industryIn this agreement, protecting the forest does not mean freezing it in time or turning it into a place where human activity is forbidden. The conservation easement was acquired from KN Forest Conservation, LLC, and allows the property to remain under private ownership. The landowner can continue sustainable forestry operations, ensuring that the woodland remains a source of timber for the local forest products industry.However, there is an important condition attached: the property cannot be subdivided or developed in ways that compromise its conservation value. The restrictions are permanent, meaning they will remain in place even if ownership of the land changes in the future.This is where conservation easements come in. Rather than purchasing an entire property and transferring ownership to a conservation organisation, a land trust can acquire specific legal rights that restrict how the land may be used. The landowner retains ownership while agreeing to protect its natural features indefinitely.In this case, the agreement also guarantees public access to the forest for non-motorised recreational activities. Visitors can continue to hike, cycle, fish, hunt, go birdwatching and observe wildlife across the property. Therefore, the forest can continue supporting the local economy while remaining accessible to people who want to enjoy the outdoors.Importance of this propertyBeyond its streams and recreational opportunities, the property has another important role to play in the region's environmental health. Part of its eastern boundary runs alongside Elk State Forest, creating a connection between large expanses of protected woodland. Maintaining these connected landscapes is important for wildlife, allowing animals to move between habitats rather than becoming isolated in increasingly fragmented patches of forest.Climate change can alter temperatures, rainfall patterns and the conditions different species need to survive. Connected forests give wildlife more room to move and find suitable habitats as their surroundings change. Moreover, the property's varied landscape, its hills, deep ravines and streamside areas create different environmental conditions, offering a range of habitats while helping the land remain resilient to climate-related changes.The forested areas around waterways, known as riparian zones, are especially important. Apart from protecting water quality, they provide shelter and movement corridors for wildlife. Keeping these areas intact helps preserve the wider ecosystem rather than protecting individual streams in isolation.The latest project is also part of a broader conservation effort across Pennsylvania. In July 2026, the Conservancy protected another 35-acre property in Ligonier Township, Westmoreland County, through a conservation easement. That land contains mature forest, farmland, an apple orchard and the Clark Hollow Natural Heritage Area, which provides habitat for a rare native shrub called buffalo-nut. These projects demonstrate how conservation agreements can protect landscapes of very different sizes and ecological importance.94 years of Western Pennsylvania ConservancyThe latest acquisition is particularly significant because it brings the Western Pennsylvania Conservancy past the 300,000-acre mark in permanently protected natural land.Founded on February 16, 1932, the organisation began as the Greater Pittsburgh Parks Association. A group of 10 citizens came together during the Great Depression, hoping to address widespread unemployment through public works programmes that would also benefit the region's natural resources.Its first on-the-ground conservation project took place in 1940 along Bigelow Boulevard in Pittsburgh. A few years later, in 1945, it began its first major land acquisition project to protect the area that would eventually become McConnells Mill State Park.Since then, its work has expanded considerably. The organisation has helped establish 11 state parks, protected or restored more than 3,000 miles of rivers and streams, and supported the preservation of thousands of wildlife species and their habitats. It also owns and operates Fallingwater, the famous house designed by architect Frank Lloyd Wright, which is now recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.The latest milestone has been made possible through contributions from the Colcom Foundation and Hillman Foundation, along with donations from member bequests and The Conservation Fund. Of the more than 300,000 acres the organisation has protected, 69,840 acres have been secured through conservation easements.For an organisation approaching its centenary, the achievement is a reminder that conservation is rarely the result of one grand gesture. It is built through individual landowners, organisations and communities making decisions that protect natural spaces over decades.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Russian national accused of surveilling US tech company
articles.summary: Russian national Igor D'iu was indicted for allegedly stalking Silicon Valley tech employees with tracking devices and fake IDs, the FBI says.
articles.body: A grand jury indicted Russian national Igor D’iu on Wednesday on charges of conspiring to act as an agent of a foreign government, acting as an agent of a foreign government without notice to the Attorney General, interstate stalking, and fraud in connection with identification documents in connection to alleged espionage of a U.S. company in Silicon Valley. "Igor D’iu was allegedly recruited, directed, and funded by the Russian government to stalk employees of a major U.S. technology company, using physical surveillance, electronic tracking devices, and fraudulent identities to gather intelligence," Roman Rozhavsky, Assistant Director of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division, said in a statement. D'iu was arrested in October after allegedly being recruited by co-conspirators through the messaging platform Telegram to clandestinely target employees of a Silicon Valley defense and technology company. FOREIGN SPY ‘HONEYTRAPS’ TARGETING AMERICA’S TECH ELITE SPARK ALARM AMID NVIDIA CEO SCANDAL D’iu's co-conspirators, who provided him with instructions, equipment, and financial support, told him his espionage was for "the Motherland," explaining that the company he was spying on was supplying weapons used against Russia in Ukraine, according to an arrest affidavit. UKRAINE RELEASES VIDEO SHOWING DAMAGE TO PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE FOLLOWING 'UNPRECEDENTED OPERATION' IN CRIMEA "Russia may rely on covert operatives and criminal intermediaries as it attempts to gain an edge in its war against Ukraine, but those tactics do not place its government or its collaborators beyond the reach of the law. This arrest should serve as a warning to anyone looking to undermine U.S. interests or threaten our national security: No matter where you are or who you’re working for, justice will find you," Rozhavsky added. D'iu is accused of entering the U.S. illegally, traveling from Istanbul, Turkey to Mexico City, Mexico in June, at which point his co-conspirators connected him with an individual who was able to smuggle him across the border. The operative was then instructed to surveil employees of the company at a Paolo Alto, California coffee shop, even directing him to attempt to remotely access information from employees' laptop computers at the cafe, according to the affidavit. The Russian national engaged in sweeping surveillance activities, including searching for employee addresses and even following a female employee for 30 miles. "The employee attempted to evade D’iu by making irregular turns, taking back roads, and entering a grocery store parking lot. D’iu allegedly aggressively continued following her, including through U-turns and illegal left turns, and ran a red light to remain behind her vehicle. Fearing for her safety, the employee called 911 and was instructed to drive to the San Francisco Police Department’s Mission Station. D’iu allegedly abandoned his pursuit after the employee contacted a police officer. Investigators also obtained evidence that D’iu had followed other company employees on preceding days," a Department of Justice statement about the indictment read. "The Americans who build our defense technology help keep this country safe by arming our warfighters with the tools and weapons they need to prevail against our adversaries and enemies," Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General M. Scott Proctor said in a statement. Such conduct, if proven, is a flagrant violation of U.S. sovereignty and an unacceptable attempt at intimidation. We will use every tool at our disposal to find, prosecute, and punish such conduct, wherever and whenever it happens," Proctor concluded. articles.title: Canada’s Carney: Trump ‘listens a lot more in private’
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Wednesday his dynamic with President Trump — fraught with public disputes — is much different behind closed doors but cautioned the U.S.-Canada relationship cannot be repaired overnight. “He’s very different inside the room, … he’s a very personable individual,” Carney told The New York Times’ Andrew Ross Sorkin at…
articles.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Wednesday his dynamic with President Trump — fraught with public disputes — is much different behind closed doors but cautioned the U.S.-Canada relationship cannot be repaired overnight.

“He’s very different inside the room, … he’s a very personable individual,” Carney told The New York Times’ Andrew Ross Sorkin at its DealBook conference in New York City. “He listens a lot more in private. I mean, he’s interested, genuinely, in your opinion, and it’s a reasonably direct conversation.”

Carney and Trump have had a tense relationship since the president returned to office.

Trump kicked off his second term saying he wanted to make Canada the 51st state, calling Carney the “governor” of Canada, adopting the name “Lake America” for Lake Ontario and levying harsh tariffs on the country after trade negotiations fell through — all of which have damaged the connection between the two allies.

The prime minister said he and Trump are “moving closer” to a deal, but they are “not yet there.”

Trump slapped 50 percent tariffs on many Canadian goods in August, even those covered under the U.S. Mexico Canada Agreement (USMCA) — the trade agreement Trump himself signed in his first term. Canada hit back with retaliatory tariffs weeks later.

The trade war began after negotiations between the two countries fell apart, and no resolution has been reached since. Trump banned $1 billion in Canadian goods from entering the U.S. in September.

Recently, Carney has suggested that Canada could pivot to China if the U.S. is no longer a reliable trading partner.

“We have the best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, full opportunity, in an integrated North American market,” Carney told reporters in Cambodia Monday. “That market has become less integrated because of U.S. trade actions.”

China and Canada struck a deal earlier this year to reduce Canadian tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles.

The Trump administration’s actions have damaged views of the U.S. among the Canadian public, too, with majorities now saying it’s not a reliable ally.

Carney said Wednesday that even when a new president takes the White House in 2029 — one who is friendlier to Canada — the two countries’ relationship may not mend right away.

“There are a host of issues where we collaborate in national security and other aspects. We still have quite an open trading relationship as well, but there are dependencies for which it would be unwise for us to not hedge,” Carney said. “I think people will be leaving on their hedges for a while until they truly believe they’re in a different market environment.”

articles.title: Police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force
articles.summary: Wales' four police chiefs were asked how they were clamping down on misconduct "in a post-Sarah Everard era".
articles.body:
The chief of Wales' largest police force says he is working to root out racists and misogynists from his organisation as part of efforts to improve trust in officers.

Chief Constable Jeremy Vaughan had responded to a question from MPs about how he and other police chiefs were clamping down on staff misconduct "in a post-Sarah Everard era".

The South Wales Police chief said: "Do I think I've got racists, misogynists, working for me? Yes. Do I think my work is to find them and excommunicate them from policing? Absolutely yes."

He appeared in front of the Welsh Affairs Committee on Wednesday, along with Wales' three other police bosses, as part of its inquiry into the future of policing.

One of the issues being examined by the committee, made up of Welsh MPs from the UK Parliament, is a UK government proposal to reduce the number of police forces in England and Wales .

Committee chairperson, Newport West and Islwyn MP Ruth Jones, had asked the chief constables of all four forces how they were evaluating their forces' performance when it came to addressing misconduct.

Jones noted in her question that "we're still in a post-Sarah Everard era", referencing the 33-year-old woman who was abducted, raped and murdered by serving Met police officer Wayne Couzens in London in 2021 , and that "there have been issues across Wales".

Vaughan said that 126 people had been dismissed from the force under his watch since he started his role six years ago, and that he believed it had been "significantly higher" than under his predecessor.

Saying he believed improvements to vetting and training meant his organisation was now "more upstanding than by-standing than ever before", he noted that 22 people within it were currently suspended - which he said was a "low proportion of the workforce".

He said that identifying and sacking racists and misogynists from within South Wales Police was a "whole-organisation leadership effort".

Dyfed-Powys Police Chief Constable Ifan Charles told the committee he had a number of people currently being investigated for gross misconduct, some of whom were currently suspended, and that "some of those are for misogynistic behaviours".

North Wales Police Chief Constable Amanda Blakeman said her force had "pursued individuals that should not be in policing" and had been "relentless in all aspects in terms of anti-corruption, information from the public, about how we'll deal with people who don't live up to" her force's standards.

Gwent Police Chief Constable Mark Hobrough admitted his force had previously had a "very different culture" with high-profile senior leaders "who did not represent the values of modern day policing" removed from it.

He said the force currently had 37 active misconduct cases and 14 people suspended.

He said a staff survey indicated high levels of confidence in reporting misconduct and that the force would deal with them.

Elsewhere in the committee the police chiefs were asked for their views on the UK government's policing White Paper published in January.

It proposes significantly reducing the number of forces in England and Wales by merging existing forces into larger ones . A review will propose the best way to organise the new forces and no final decisions have yet been taken.

Wales currently has four forces, but there has been speculation it could go down to one, as is the case in Northern Ireland and Scotland.

Blakeman told MPs she thought the current structure should remain in place.

"I'm genuinely concerned about the prospect of force mergers because of that difference that we see in north Wales, and I'm concerned about the impact that those mergers may have in terms of our communities and the service they get," she said.

"Anything that is centralised tends to see service reduced in our rural communities, of which there is a large scale across north Wales."

She said delivering for rural communities would be "significantly at risk" if Wales went down to one force.

"I'm concerned about the vulnerability and isolation that we would see in the furthest part of north Wales that's disconnected from the point of view of road infrastructure, ability to travel, and is more connected to the North West of England," she added.

Vaughan said a restructure of forces could deliver efficiencies but must be properly funded.

He said he broadly agreed with the "direction of travel" set out in the government's proposals.

But added: "It's quite hard to analyse the specifics because I don't know what they are yet."

The UK government has been approached for comment.

articles.title: Carney: Trump not concerned about growing Canada trade ties with China
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Wednesday that President Trump is not worried about Ottawa’s deepening trade ties with China. “In my conversation with the president, he’s tried to understand where we are with China, where we’re going with China, but it’s not — I wouldn’t — I shouldn’t speak for him, but in his…
articles.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Wednesday that President Trump is not worried about Ottawa’s deepening trade ties with China.

“In my conversation with the president, he’s tried to understand where we are with China, where we’re going with China, but it’s not — I wouldn’t — I shouldn’t speak for him, but in his hierarchy of issues, it’s not the top issue at all,” Carney told reporters while in China.

Earlier this year, Trump said that Carney should go through with a trade deal with Beijing.

“That’s OK. That’s what he should be doing. I mean, it’s a good thing for him to sign a trade deal. If you can get a deal with China, you should do that,” Trump said when asked about what he thought of the trade deal at the time.

In January, Canada and China came to an initial trade deal, getting rid of tariffs on electric vehicles and canola. The Associated Press reported that Canada would initially let in a maximum of 48,000 Chinese electric vehicles with a 6.1 percent tariff. Beijing was expected to then bring down its tariff on canola seed by early March.

Carney’s Wednesday comments also follow recent trade tension between Ottawa and Washington, with both countries slapping tariffs on each other’s goods.

On Saturday, Carney said trade negotiations between Ottawa and the U.S. were progressing. He told reporters in Manila that he had a discussion with Trump, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, White House chief of staff Stephen Miller and other officials “just before” going to the Philippines for the Association of the Southeast Asian Nations’ (ASEAN) summit. The Canadian prime minister added that Canada and the U.S. were “making progress.”

Carney also stressed Saturday that he would not “settle for a deal” not in line with “a viable Canadian auto sector.”

articles.title: After losing his  daughter Kiran, Rajasthan's Shyam Sundar Paliwal started planting 111 trees for every girl born in his village; in 2021 he received the Padma Shri for his work
articles.summary: Every girl child born in this village of Rajasthan is celebrated with the planting of 111 trees in her name.
articles.body: Every girl child born in this village of Rajasthan is celebrated with the planting of 111 trees in her name. Now this is one ritual that brings hope and environmental conservation. Welcome to Piplantri village where a girl child is not seen as a financial responsibility. Instead, the girl’s arrival becomes a festival and 111 trees are planted in her honour. The little girl grows up with the trees, becoming a living reminder that her life is valued.Welcome to Piplantri village in RajasthanPiplantri village is located in Rajsamand district of Rajasthan. But planting trees is a tradition that has an emotional story behind. It began when a father lost his daughter at a young age. He planted 111 trees in her name and this gradually became a community movement.Meet Shyam Sundar Paliwal, the man behind this commendable initiativeThe man behind the initiative is Shyam Sundar Paliwal, a former village sarpanch. According to a United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) report on panchayats leading the way in women's empowerment, Paliwal's daughter Kiran died in 2006 due to dehydration caused by extreme heat. It was a loss that left him devastated.He planted a Kadamb tree in her memory. However, it soon became the starting point of a much larger mission.This was the time when Piplantri was struggling with many challenges. Excessive marble mining had contributed to deforestation, while water scarcity and deteriorating environmental conditions affected the village. There was also a need to address the social attitudes that often made families consider daughters a burden.Paliwal became the village sarpanch in 2005. He believed that the arrival of a girl should be celebrated just as warmly as the birth of a boy. It was he who proposed a simple idea: whenever a girl was born in Piplantri, the community would plant 111 trees in her name.Paliwal's contribution to environmental conservation and social work also earned him the Padma Shri in 2021, in the Social Work category. Taking to Instagram, he shared the picture and wrote,"I am truly blessed to receive the Padma Shri Award from our Honourable President of India.I am extremely grateful and honoured. 🙏🏻"Securing a daughter's future with Kiran Nidhi YojanaHowever, Paliwal understood that planting trees alone would not change the way society looked at daughters. For the initiative to make a lasting difference, families also needed to feel financially secure about their girls' futures.This led to the introduction of the Kiran Nidhi Yojana, named after his daughter. Under the original arrangement, the parents contributed Rs 10,000, while the village community contributed another Rs 21,000. The combined amount of Rs 31,000 was deposited as a fixed deposit in the name of the newborn girl, with the money intended to support her future.However, the financial assistance came with a commitment with a stamp paper signature by parents promising:They would not practise female foeticideThey ensure their daughter received an educationThey would not marry her off before she turned 18They pledged to take care of the 111 trees planted in her nameRaksha Bandhan ritualAnother important ritual here includes, every year, on Raksha Bandhan, girls in the village tie rakhis around the trees. It’s a gesture symbolising their bond with the saplings. As the girls grow older, they are encouraged to look after the trees, treating them as family members.The responsibility, however, does not rest entirely with the girls. The village panchayat, women from self-help groups and other community members have also played a role in nurturing the plantation. Government employment schemes have been used to support the maintenance of the green spaces, creating work opportunities while protecting the trees.The aloe vera initiativeRainwater harvesting structures and other measures were introduced to help sustain the plantation in an area that had struggled with water scarcity. The village also began planting aloe vera around trees to protect them from termites. Over time, processing aloe vera into products such as juice, gel and pickles created additional livelihood opportunities for local women.From a father's grief to an international exampleAccording to the United Nations Sustainable Development Group, which documented the Piplantri model in October 2022, the village had nearly 400,000 trees. This is an average of around 50 girls being born there every year.The model has attracted international as well as attention from other villages and development organisations. It demonstrates how a community-led initiative can connect environmental conservation with social development rather than treating them as separate challenges.Today, every newborn girl in the village represents an opportunity to plant 111 trees, invest in an education and make a promise for the future. And perhaps that is the most meaningful part of Paliwal's initiative: the trees are not simply a tribute to his daughter Kiran; they are a reminder to an entire community that every girl deserves the chance to grow.You use AI every day. articles.title: Florence Pugh denies Ozempic and plastic surgery claims in a lengthy Instagram post: 'Here's the truth'
articles.summary: Florence Pugh says she's focused on building strength and taking care of herself, pushing back against strangers dissecting her appearance.
articles.body:
Florence Pugh has spent years defending her body against criticism. Now, she's defending her face — and her right to have her appearance change.

After her appearance at the Academy's Governors Awards on Nov. 15 sparked speculation about cosmetic procedures, the 30-year-old pushed back in a lengthy Instagram post . She denies facial surgery and Ozempic use, questioning why strangers feel entitled to dissect her appearance.

"I find it so stressful waking up and [having] thousands of people talking about you and your body in ways that you can't even comprehend," she wrote. "I woke up the other morning and quite a lot of you were discussing my face and body in such a disturbing way."

The commentary ranged from accusations of the actor getting cosmetic surgery — an upper or lower bleph? Buccal fat removal? — to guesses that she might have lost weight with the help of a GLP-1.

"I have never been on ozempic. I have NEVER done any face surgery. And don't EVER say that I didn't make my own nose, I've always had that beautiful ski slope. Even as a baby!" wrote Pugh.

The East of Eden star's statement comes after speculation swept across social media. One Instagram video posted by Evie magazine on Tuesday compared older and newer photos of Pugh and suggested she had "fallen victim to Hollywood's obsession with sculpted faces."

Pugh responded directly beneath the video later that day.

"Guys. I turned 30. I'm a woman. Body's and faces change. It's not that deep, the fact that people can't even tell between what's aging and what's surgery is disturbing," she wrote. "Sadly puppy fluff doesn't last forever."

Still, onlookers continued to discuss her changing looks — and their skepticism that natural aging is responsible for it. "I love her but the Botox and fillers are so obvious, I miss her old face so much," wrote one Redditor .

"I have spent my whole career defending and protecting bodies that just grow the way they grow. I was subjected to fat shaming in the business from the moment I started and I have loved everytime I get to tell someone to f*** off when they are being inappropriate about my weight, and I'm not changing that now just because you've all said so."

"Here's the truth," Pugh added, sharing that turning 30 prompted resolutions to change her relationship with alcohol and to train with the goal of completing a pull-up. "For the first time in my ENTIRE career, I have had the opportunity to be rested, to sleep, to wake up and work out and to eat regularly and healthily. I've WANTED to move my body and not take it for granted," she wrote. "Guess how much weight I've lost in all of that? 2 pounds."

More importantly, she's gained strength and has surpassed her pull-up goal with the help of a trainer. "I can now do 6 pull ups," she continued. "I'm looking after myself, and that's literally it."

The Dune: Part Three star went on to describe years of contradictory criticism: strangers calling her fat, telling her to take Ozempic and insisting that she shouldn't show her midriff.

"I've always been aware that seeing a confident woman be happy in her skin is triggering to a lot of people and for [a] long time just accepted that I will receive commentary like that. But now this…?"

She also revealed she had "sued a few publications" earlier this year for publishing AI images that seemed to show her getting injectables. "They lied to sell their story. But it damaged me," she wrote.

Even commentary presented as concern about beauty standards subjects her body to scrutiny, she reminded followers. "I understand that we are in a warped part of image history right now, with beauty standards changing, getting harder and harder to keep up with," she wrote. "But please be gentle with yourselves and others when you go in on people's physical appearance."

House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) is hosting a ceremony on Wednesday to posthumously award former Egyptian President Anwar Sadat the Congressional Gold Medal , the legislative branch’s highest civilian honor.

Sadat is being recognized for his historic efforts to advance peace in the Middle East, including the 1978 Camp David Accords and the 1979 peace treaty between Egypt and Israel. He was assassinated in 1981.

Members of Sadat’s family and Egyptian officials are expected to attend the ceremony at the U.S. Capitol.

The event is scheduled to begin at 3 p.m. EST.
